title: Natural Domain and Graph of a Downward-Opening Parabola
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Domain and Graphing
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain and describe the graph of the quadratic function f(x) = 1 - 2x - x^2.

steps.title: Determine the Natural Domain
steps.explanation: As a quadratic polynomial, f(x) = 1 - 2x - x^2 involves only multiplication and addition/subtraction, so its natural domain is (-inf, inf).
steps.why: Every polynomial function has natural domain equal to the set of all real numbers.

steps.title: Complete the Square to Locate the Vertex
steps.explanation: Factor -1 from the x^2 and x terms, add and subtract 1 to complete the square (x + 1)^2, and rewrite f(x) in vertex form as 2 - (x + 1)^2.
steps.why: Vertex form a(x - h)^2 + k immediately reveals the vertex (h, k) and axis of symmetry x = h.

steps.title: Identify Intercepts and Sketch the Parabola
steps.explanation: The graph is a downward-opening parabola with maximum at its vertex (-1, 2), symmetric about the vertical line x = -1, crossing the y-axis at (0, 1) and the x-axis at x = -1 - sqrt(2) and x = -1 + sqrt(2).
steps.why: Because the leading coefficient a = -1 is negative, the parabola opens downward from its vertex.
